newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan plans interim dividend next year.
newsitem.headline: Nissan plans interim dividend next year.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd plans to resume paying an interim dividend in its next business year, company president Yoshikazu Hanawa told a news conference on Tuesday.
But Nissan has not decided how large the half-year dividend will be, Hanawa said.
Japan's second-biggest carmaker has made no interim dividend payment since 1992/93, but it has been paying a full-year dividend of seven yen since 1993/94.
Hanawa also said Nissan wants to boost its domestic market share to 25 percent in 2000 and 30 percent before 2010.
Nissan's earlier forecast domestic sales of 1.16 million vehicles in 1997, up 3.7 percent from this year, which would give it a 21.7 percent market share if overall sales forecasts remain unchanged.
Its 1996 market share is estimated at 21 percent, which would be lower than its previous low of 21.2 percent in 1994.
Nissan will introduce eight remodelled or new models next year, mainly recreational vehicles, Hanawa said.
The company will also offer a continuously variable transmission in its 2.0 litre-engined cars next summer, Hanawa said. The transmission cuts fuel consumption.
Hanawa also said Nissan will introduce a direct-injection gasoline engine by the end of 1997.
The engine uses less fuel and produces less carbon dioxide as engine combustion is controlled more precisely.
